- `B005-F06-009`: — <code>symbol_file_payload</code> schema (lines 114-120): file is primary key; persist language, blake3 content hash, MessagePack symbols, and MessagePack edges. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:259)_
- `B005-F06-010`: — <code>symbol_graph_meta</code> schema (lines 121-131): key by project ID and store symbol/edge/file counts, unresolved-edge percentage, injected-clock <code>built_at</code>, and schema version; migration is v3 and adds no SQLite dependency. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:260)_
- `B005-F06-011`: — symbol domain types (lines 133-140): <code>SymbolKind</code> values are Function, Method, Class, Struct, Trait, Module, Enum, Interface, Type; <code>SymbolNode</code>, <code>SymbolEdge</code>, <code>SymbolRef</code>, and <code>EntryPoint</code> have the exact fields stated, and all serialize through serde/MessagePack. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:261)_
- `B005-F06-012`: — confidence model (lines 136-138): <code>Confidence</code> is exactly <code>Local|Unique|MultipleCandidates|Unresolved</code>; each edge also carries candidate IDs and a <code>CallSite</code>. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:262)_
- `B005-F06-013`: — sharding functions (lines 142-145): <code>name_shard_key</code> returns the first lowercase ASCII letter or underscore; <code>reverse_shard_bucket</code> returns first SHA1 byte of file; <code>all_name_shard_keys()</code> returns all 27 keys. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:263)_
- `B005-F06-014`: — extraction contract (lines 147-155): <code>extract_symbols_and_calls(source, language, file)</code> uses existing tree-sitter grammars, not ast-grep; raw calls contain caller ID, callee name, and call site; every file gets a synthetic <code>&lt;module&gt;</code> caller for unattributed calls. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:264)_
- `B005-F06-015`: — resolver tiers (lines 156-165): resolution searches same-file Local, one-hop Imported, then two-hop Re-export dependencies; zero candidates yields Unresolved, one Unique, and multiple MultipleCandidates; mutate <code>outgoing_calls_by_file</code> in place. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:265)_
- `B005-F06-016`: — eager metadata/lazy indexes (lines 166-177): <code>SymbolGraphCache</code> eagerly holds tiny metadata; first name query loads 27 shards in parallel through <code>tokio::JoinSet</code>; first impact query loads 256 reverse shards in parallel; file payloads are lazy. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:266)_
- `B005-F06-017`: — LRU implementation/capacity (lines 176-181): cache at most 500 <code>Arc&lt;SymbolGraphFilePayload&gt;</code> entries; implement a tiny LRU with existing/standard facilities and obtain explicit confirmation before any new dependency; constructor accepts project ID, SQLite pool, and configurable capacity. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:267)_
- `B005-F06-018`: — impact traversal API (lines 183-192): <code>compute_impact_radius(cache,target,depth)</code> recognizes file path versus symbol name, BFSes the reverse-file index, returns deterministic <code>BTreeMap&lt;u32,Vec&lt;String&gt;&gt;</code> hop bands plus <code>truncated</code>, and clamps depth to ten. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:268)_
- `B005-F06-019`: — call-flow API (lines 193-198): <code>compute_call_flow</code> performs cycle-aware DFS, loads child payloads only while descending, clamps depth to ten, and annotates leaves with <code>TruncationReason::Depth|Cycle</code>. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:269)_
- `B005-F06-020`: — symbol-context API (lines 199-202): <code>compute_symbol_context(cache,name,file_hint)</code> returns every matching definition, not only the first, with callers/callees and confidence; file hint disambiguates. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:270)_
- `B005-F06-021`: — symbol-list API (lines 203-204): <code>list_symbols</code> filters by optional file, optional query, and required limit. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:271)_
- `B005-F06-022`: — invalidation boundary (lines 206-210): <code>invalidate_file(file)</code> evicts its payload and marks name/reverse indexes for partial rebuild; more than fifty changed files forces a full rebuild. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:272)_
- `B005-F06-023`: — full build lifecycle (lines 212-223): after DKG build, extract each file, resolve against the import graph, build deterministic shard maps, persist all four table families as MessagePack, and log files/symbols/edges/unresolved percentage. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:273)_
- `B005-F06-024`: — incremental build lifecycle (lines 225-229): when changed count is at most <code>INCREMENTAL_SYMBOL_THRESHOLD</code>, patch changed/removed payloads and only affected name/reverse buckets; otherwise rebuild fully. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:274)_
- `B005-F06-025`: — dispatcher schemas (lines 231-243): register <code>symbol_impact {target,depth?}</code>, <code>symbol_flow {entrypoint?,file?,depth?}</code>, <code>symbol_context {name,file?}</code>, and <code>symbol_list {file?,query?,limit?}</code>; flow without an entrypoint lists B-34 candidates if available, otherwise errors. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:275)_
- `B005-F06-026`: — Auditor auto-injection (lines 245-250): in PostToolUse Write/Edit, for every changed file call impact at depth two; if any files are impacted, append <code>IMPACT_SUMMARY</code> to the Auditor briefing. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:276)_
- `B005-F06-027`: — query event schema (lines 252-254): append <code>symbol_query</code> per query with <code>{tool,target,hop_count,total_files,latency_ms}</code> for dashboard activity. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:277)_
- `B005-F06-028`: — dashboard impact panel (lines 256-260): KnowledgeDrawer shows unresolved-edge percentage, last target/depth/total/hop table, and a <code>/symbol_impact</code> input routed through synthetic <code>submit_task</code> intent. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:278)_
- `B005-F06-029`: — produced symbol registry (lines 262-278): export cache/traversal/resolution/extraction/sharding functions, <code>SsbActionType::SymbolQuery</code>, and IPC constants <code>TOOL_SYMBOL_IMPACT</code>, <code>TOOL_SYMBOL_FLOW</code>, <code>TOOL_SYMBOL_CONTEXT</code>, <code>TOOL_SYMBOL_LIST</code>. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:279)_
- `B005-F06-030`: — integration registry (lines 279-293): full/update indexing call graph builds; TaskRunner PostToolUse performs depth-two impact; dashboard <code>get_impact_analysis</code> reads meta/hops; CLI research uses symbol context; paths are reachable from CLI, dashboard, and TaskRunner. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:280)_
- `B005-F06-031`: — cache/data stub bans (lines 294-300): first impact query must really load reverse index when metadata reports edges; LRU capacity must be 500; ELAI’s unresolved-edge percentage must be below 50%, with below 30% ideal but not mandatory. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:281)_
- `B005-F06-032`: — frontend dependency (lines 301-302): B-33 is the frontend pair and consumes the same cache for symbol-mode visualization. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:282)_
- `B005-F06-033`: — observable contract (lines 303-307): the four-tool dispatch smoke writes one <code>symbol_query</code> row per tool and stdout must contain a real “Hop 1” block with ELAI paths. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:283)_
- `B005-F06-034`: — database acceptance bounds (lines 309-325): all four tables must exist; ELAI meta requires at least 5,000 symbols, 8,000 edges, and under 50% unresolved; reverse index must contain a known multi-caller clock entry. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:284)_
- `B005-F06-035`: — CLI behavioral checks (lines 326-341): impact on <code>ClockProvider</code> should return depth three and at least twenty files; flow from CLI <code>main</code> should show a real call tree; an edit rename task must yield an Auditor <code>IMPACT_SUMMARY</code> with at least five dependent files. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:285)_
- `B005-F06-036`: — boundedness check (lines 343-345): after one thousand payload accesses, LRU size remains at most 500, covered by <code>test_lru_capacity_bounded</code>. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:286)_
- `B005-F06-037`: — acceptance gates (lines 348-366): property-test depth/cycles/target polymorphism, persist 27/256 shards, make v3 idempotent, integrate full/incremental indexing, expose all four tools through CLI/dashboard/IPC, inject impact, emit latency telemetry, render real UI, use no non-test unwrap, and add no unconfirmed dependency. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:287)_
- `B005-F06-038`: — extraction/resolution tests (lines 368-375): fixtures cover Rust/Python/TS/Go/JVM counts/names and Local/Imported/Re-export call sites with asserted confidence. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:288)_
- `B005-F06-039`: — cache/traversal tests (lines 376-383): test capacity, parallel shard loading, payload eviction/index preservation, depth bounds, cycle termination, all-match context, and list limits. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:289)_
- `B005-F06-040`: — end-to-end/contracts (lines 384-387): add IPC <code>symbol_query_dispatch.rs</code> and <code>tests/contracts/symbol_graph_contract.rs</code> for meta/schema sanity. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:290)_
- `B005-F06-041`: — implementation footprint (lines 389-412): create the complete <code>knowledge::symbol_graph</code> module set, store and migration; modify knowledge export, indexing, dispatcher, TaskRunner, SSB action types, V2 Tauri, KnowledgeDrawer; create <code>B-29-decisions.md</code>. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:291)_
- `B005-F06-042`: — required decisions (lines 414-427): document SQLite MessagePack shards, std-only LRU, in-place confidence mutation, always-on versus feature-gated <code>IMPACT_SUMMARY</code> (recommend always-on with env opt-out), default/user depth, and FocalAD as the design anchor. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:292)_
- `B005-F06-043`: — unlocked capabilities (lines 429-442): provide evidence-based edit scope, existing-project call-flow grounding, authoritative Oracle caller answers, B-23 blast-radius signals, and zero-extra-load B-33/B-34 reuse. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:293)_
- `B005-F06-044`: — downstream (lines 444-448): B-30 is independent; B-33 waits for the cache; B-34 waits for file payloads. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:294)_
- `SUMMARY/SUM-0214`: section=`B-29 - Symbol-level impact analysis API - PLANNED; highest-leverage recommendation` Four agent-callable operations use a sharded, LRU-bounded `SymbolGraphCache`: `compute_impact_radius` does reverse-call BFS with hop bands and depth <=10; `compute_call_flow` does cycle-aware DFS with lazy children and depth <=10; `compute_symbol_context` returns definition plus confidence-tagged callers/callees; `list_symbols` filters by file/query/limit. _(anchor: 02-B-PLAN-SUMMARY.discovery.md:373)_
- `SUMMARY/SUM-0215`: section=`B-29 - Symbol-level impact analysis API - PLANNED; highest-leverage recommendation` Cache layout: 27 name shards (`a-z` plus `_`), 256 reverse shards keyed by single-byte SHA1 prefix, and a 500-file payload LRU. A query must never load every symbol or edge. _(anchor: 02-B-PLAN-SUMMARY.discovery.md:374)_
- `SUMMARY/SUM-0216`: section=`B-29 - Symbol-level impact analysis API - PLANNED; highest-leverage recommendation` Resolver confidence is one of `Local`, `Imported` (one hop), `Re-export` (two hops), or `Unresolved`. _(anchor: 02-B-PLAN-SUMMARY.discovery.md:375)_
- `SUMMARY/SUM-0217`: section=`B-29 - Symbol-level impact analysis API - PLANNED; highest-leverage recommendation` DKG schema v3 tables are `symbol_name_index`, `symbol_reverse_index`, `symbol_file_payload`, and `symbol_graph_meta`, with MessagePack BLOBs. _(anchor: 02-B-PLAN-SUMMARY.discovery.md:376)_
- `SUMMARY/SUM-0218`: section=`B-29 - Symbol-level impact analysis API - PLANNED; highest-leverage recommendation` Dispatcher entries are `symbol_impact`, `symbol_flow`, `symbol_context`, `symbol_list`. _(anchor: 02-B-PLAN-SUMMARY.discovery.md:377)_
- `SUMMARY/SUM-0219`: section=`B-29 - Symbol-level impact analysis API - PLANNED; highest-leverage recommendation` Auditor `PostToolUse` auto-injects `IMPACT_SUMMARY` at depth two for changed files. _(anchor: 02-B-PLAN-SUMMARY.discovery.md:378)_
- `SUMMARY/SUM-0220`: section=`B-29 - Symbol-level impact analysis API - PLANNED; highest-leverage recommendation` Fewer than fifty changed files triggers incremental invalidation; more than fifty triggers full rebuild. _(anchor: 02-B-PLAN-SUMMARY.discovery.md:379)_
- `SUMMARY/SUM-0221`: section=`B-29 - Symbol-level impact analysis API - PLANNED; highest-leverage recommendation` Implement LRU using std only, with no `lru` crate. FocalAD (`arXiv:2506.11419`) is the stated research anchor for top-k local focus. _(anchor: 02-B-PLAN-SUMMARY.discovery.md:380)_

### B-29.5: Symbol-graph scale benchmark (release gate)
- **Status:** planned
- **Anchors:** `B29S-001` @ DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:229; `B29S-002` @ DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:230; `B29S-003` @ DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:231; `B29S-004` @ DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:232; `B29S-005` @ DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:233; `B29S-006` @ DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:234; `B29S-007` @ DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:235; `B29S-008` @ DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:236; `B29S-009` @ DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:237; `B29S-010` @ DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:238
- **Composes with:**
  - `B-004/X-E06` ↔ B-25, B-31.5: B-31.5 reuses B-29.5’s exact fixtures, can run in parallel, and explicitly turns B-25’s Empire-corpus claim into a testable scale assertion (B-31.5 L10-L13, L475-L499).
  - `B-006/INT-013` ↔ B-29, B-31, B-31.5: : B-29.5 is an evidence gate over B-29 traversal/cache claims and depends on B-31 resume; B-31.5 shares fixtures but measures an orthogonal indexing domain (B29.5 lines 1-12, 192-209, 458-461).
  - `B-006/INT-020` ↔ B-29, B-30, B-35: : B-29.5’s per-language unresolved-edge evidence can prioritize B-30 extractor work and can improve the B-29 symbol context paired with B-35, but neither benchmark completion nor artifact completion directly implements the other (B29.5 line
  - `B29S-002` → B-29, B-31, B-31.5: Dependencies/parallelism: B-29 and resumable B-31 are prerequisites; B-31.5 may run in parallel and share fixtures (lines 8-12).
  - `B29S-019` → B-31: Recovery dependency: Linux/Chromium indexing is expected to take one to three hours and must use B-31 resume after interruption (lines 207-209, 324-329).
- `B29S-001`: Scope: The benchmark must prove B-29’s cache and four traversals at Linux-kernel, Chromium, VS Code, and PostgreSQL scale without OOM, with p99 below 500ms and stable hop-banded output (lines 1-7). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:229)_
- `B29S-002`: Dependencies/parallelism: B-29 and resumable B-31 are prerequisites; B-31.5 may run in parallel and share fixtures (lines 8-12). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:230)_
- `B29S-003`: Risk thesis: Sharding, LRU payload bounds, hop-banded BFS, and lazy DFS were only proven on about 140K LOC/8,075 nodes; the benchmark must establish that no query loads the full graph and memory follows result-set size rather than total graph size (lines 14-37). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:231)_
- `B29S-004`: External-evidence boundary: SocratiCode’s 40M-LOC claim is treated as unverified because its located test is about 200K symbols/10K files; ELAI must generate its own evidence (lines 24-27). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:232)_
- `B29S-005`: Research anchor: FocalAD ELAI arXiv:2506.11419 supports top-k local-focus selection, while this benchmark is explicitly the engineering bounded-memory/latency proof (lines 39-45). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:233)_
- `B29S-006`: Fixture root: Fixtures live outside .elai_cc at configurable ELAI_SCALE_FIXTURE_ROOT, defaulting to a home-directory elai_scale_fixtures path; this prevents ordinary project indexing from ingesting them (lines 64-78). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:234)_
- `B29S-007`: Linux fixture: clone_scale_fixtures.sh shallow-clones torvalds/linux v6.7, approximately 36M LOC and primarily C/asm (lines 79-81, 99-104). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:235)_
- `B29S-008`: Chromium fixture: The script shallow-clones chromium/src 121.0.6167.184 without depot_tools, approximately 35M LOC and mixed C++/JS/TS/Python/ObjC (lines 82-85, 105-110). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:236)_
- `B29S-009`: VS Code fixture: The script shallow-clones microsoft/vscode 1.94.2, approximately 2.45M LOC of TS/JS/CSS/HTML (lines 86-88, 111-116). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:237)_
- `B29S-010`: PostgreSQL fixture: The script shallow-clones postgres REL_17_0, approximately 1.5M LOC of C/Perl/Tcl/SQL/shell (lines 89-91, 117-122). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:238)_
- `B29S-011`: Reproducible acquisition: Fixture tags/commits are pinned, existing directories are not recloned, and phase_b29_5_fixture_inventory.toml records paths, pins, exact measured LOC, and languages to prevent HEAD drift (lines 70-122). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:239)_
- `B29S-012`: Criterion harness: symbol_graph_scale.rs benchmarks impact_radius, call_flow, symbol_context, and list_symbols separately per tier/tool with criterion sample_size 20 and fixed high-fan-in symbols (lines 124-165). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:240)_
- `B29S-013`: Per-language diagnosis: Separating each tier/tool combination exposes degradation such as template-heavy C++ resolution versus plain C (lines 163-165). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:241)_
- `B29S-014`: Memory snapshot schema: MemorySnapshot records rss_bytes, heap_bytes, cache_lru_size, name_index_loaded, and reverse_index_loaded (lines 167-178). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:242)_
- `B29S-015`: Memory instrumentation: RSS uses procfs on Linux and GetProcessMemoryInfo on Windows. Heap may use jemalloc-ctl only if jemalloc is already global; adding it requires user approval (lines 179-181). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:243)_
- `B29S-016`: Realistic workload: The workload is exactly 1,000 queries: 60% impact_radius depth 2-3, 25% symbol_context, 10% call_flow, and 5% list_symbols, starting from a cold-loaded cache (lines 183-190). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:244)_
- `B29S-017`: Workload metrics: Each tool records p50/p95/p99, plus LRU hit rate, peak memory, and final file_payload_lru size, which must be <= 500 (lines 189-190, 219-229). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:245)_
- `B29S-018`: Indexing evidence: All four fixtures are indexed with per-tier metrics covering wall time, peak indexing RSS, node/edge counts per language, symbol_count, edge_count, file_count, and unresolved_edge_pct (lines 192-209). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:246)_
- `B29S-019`: Recovery dependency: Linux/Chromium indexing is expected to take one to three hours and must use B-31 resume after interruption (lines 207-209, 324-329). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:247)_
- `B29S-020`: Benchmark artifact: Criterion JSON is written to phase_b29_5_bench_raw.json, expected valid and over 100KB with tier × tool entries (lines 211-218, 338-341). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:248)_
- `B29S-021`: Repeat determinism: The bench runs twice; a target must return identical total_files and identical hop-band sets, with cross-run variance below 10% for the reported p99 observation (lines 216-218, 305-310). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:249)_
- `B29S-022`: Aggregate schema: phase_b29_5_scale.toml records per-tier index counts/timing/shard sizes and nested workload query count, hit rate, peak RSS, and per-tool quantiles (lines 231-256). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:250)_
- `B29S-023`: Five-run regression proof: symbol_graph_determinism runs impact_radius five times and requires byte-identical BTreeMap<u32, Vec<String>> plus identical truncated flags for linux::kmalloc, vscode::vscode_extension, chromium::BrowserMain, and postgres::PortalRunMulti (lines 258-267). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:251)_
- `B29S-024`: CI performance guard: scale_p99_budget_contract reads populated metrics, requires every tool/tier p99 <= 500ms, LRU memory <= 2GB on a 16GB-equivalent machine, and unresolved_edge_pct <= 50% (lines 268-273). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:252)_
- `B29S-025`: Reproduction record: phase_b29_5_README documents exact pins, sample size, target CPU/RAM/storage, and expected per-tier wall time (lines 275-280). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:253)_
- `B29S-026`: Wiring contract: Produced symbols are the criterion harness, MemorySnapshot/snapshot, run_realistic_workload, determinism regression, and p99 CI contract; they consume SymbolGraphCache, all four B-29 traversals, and B-29/B-31 indexing (lines 282-295). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:254)_
- `B29S-027`: Reachability/resource gate: The bench is reached by cargo bench; scale tests are include-ignored because fixtures must be pre-cloned. The CI contract must read populated data and fixture cloning must use pins (lines 295-304). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:255)_
- `B29S-028`: OS-visible observation: A completed run must populate scale metrics and show stable p99 across two runs with <10% variance (lines 305-310). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:256)_
- `B29S-029`: Deterministic done gates: Checks cover pinned HEADs, four resumable indices, nonempty symbol_graph_meta, JSON criterion output, the 500ms contract, five-run hop-band identity, and <=2048MB Chromium workload RSS (lines 312-355). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:257)_
- `B29S-030`: Acceptance performance bounds: Every traversal on every tier must meet p99 <=500ms; a 1,000-query workload must remain <=2GB peak RSS; Linux should have about 5M+ DKG nodes/2M+ symbols and overall unresolved edges below 50% (lines 357-375). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:258)_
- `B29S-031`: Language-quality evidence: Per-language unresolved_edge_pct is documented but not gated because C/C++ dynamic dispatch/macros are expected to be worse than TS/JS (lines 376-378). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:259)_
- `B29S-032`: Failure escalation: Any tier that misses p99 reopens B-29 and requires a decision record; failure may not be silently accepted (lines 379-380). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:260)_
- `B29S-033`: Dependency permission: No external crate, including jemalloc/procfs candidates, may be added without explicit user confirmation (lines 381-382). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:261)_
- `B29S-034`: Required artifacts: The source enumerates the clone script, three bench/workload modules, two tests, fixture/scale/readme/per-tier metrics, and B-29.5-decisions (lines 384-410). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:262)_
- `B29S-035`: Official-run policy: The decision record must choose official hardware, preserve host-specific sibling metrics rather than overwrite official numbers, and decide full-four-tier gating versus the recommended Linux+VS Code minimum (lines 412-423). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:263)_
- `B29S-036`: Budget/scheduling policy: The decision record must justify 500ms, document user-facing hook cost, choose memory instrumentation, and schedule the multi-hour benchmark nightly rather than per commit (lines 424-435). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:264)_
- `B29S-037`: Secondary outcomes: Published metrics ground performance claims, identify weak B-30 extractors, share fixtures with B-31.5/B-30, and expose C++ extraction regressions (lines 437-449). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:265)_
- `B29S-038`: Explicit non-goal: Auditor signal-to-noise for impact results is not measured here; it is only a future self-modification signal candidate (lines 450-456). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:266)_
- `B29S-039`: Lifecycle: B-31.5 uses the same fixtures for an orthogonal metric domain and may run in parallel (lines 458-461). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:267)_
- `B29S-040`: Fixture database path: The symbol-graph check uses {fixture}/.elai_cc/.elai_cc/indexes/dkg.db (lines 331-335); the duplicated directory segment is not explained and must be reconciled with the actual B-1/B-31 layout before automation. _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:268)_
- `B29S-041`: Threshold boundary: The objective says p99 “under 500ms,” while contracts and acceptance use <= 500ms (lines 5, 270, 345, 366). The exact equality boundary is internally inconsistent. _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:269)_
- `B29S-042`: Status: No shipped overlay exists and all acceptance rows are unchecked, so this source is a planned benchmark/release-evidence gate rather than measured proof (lines 357-382). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:270)_

  - `B-006/INT-014` ↔ B-31, B-35: : B-35 depends on B-31’s lock lifecycle and B-32’s line/character chunkers; the exact artifact lock scope remains open (B35 lines 9-13, 181-185, 210-215).

  - `B005-F07-028` → B-29, B-31, B-35: — downstream (lines 373-379): B-31 shares the refactor, B-29 is independent, and B-35 reuses the chunker for artifacts.
- `B005-F07-001`: — objective/dependencies (lines 1-10): prevent minified, vendored, packed, and generated one-line files from exceeding embedding context or creating useless BM25 chunks by adding deterministic detection and a universal cap; estimate three to five hours, require B-1, bundle naturally with B-31, and allow B-29/B-30/B-31/B-33/B-34/B-35 in parallel. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:316)_
- `B005-F07-002`: — baseline quality (lines 12-18): existing Phase-3K tree-sitter chunking uses function/impl/struct/class regions with fifty-line fallback and reports R@5 0.6333 and R@10 0.7667 on thirty queries. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:317)_
- `B005-F07-003`: — failure chain (lines 20-36): valid one-line JS/CSS/generated code parses as one giant AST region; 50K+ payloads exceed provider context or become noisy, while BM25 accepts semantically poor chunks; current cap occurs only at the provider boundary. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:318)_
- `B005-F07-004`: — pre-strategy detector (lines 38-44): compute average content length per line; a strict value above 500 routes immediately to character chunking and skips AST. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:319)_
- `B005-F07-005`: — universal safety net (lines 46-52): after AST, line-window, or character chunking, enforce <code>MAX_CHUNK_CHARS = 2000</code> before provider pretruncation. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:320)_
- `B005-F07-006`: — safe splitting/identity (lines 54-58): character chunking scans backward for newline, space, tab, semicolon, or comma and identifies chunks by byte offset rather than line number. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:321)_
- `B005-F07-007`: — constants (lines 80-92): define <code>MAX_AVG_LINE_LENGTH: usize = 500</code> and <code>MAX_CHUNK_CHARS: usize = 2000</code>; the latter must stay under embedding tokens times chars-per-token. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:322)_
- `B005-F07-008`: — detector function (lines 94-103): <code>is_minified(content,line_count)</code> returns <code>content.len() &gt; 500</code> when line count is zero, otherwise integer-divided <code>content.len()/line_count &gt; 500</code>; caller supplies the count to avoid allocation. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:323)_
- `B005-F07-009`: — character API (lines 105-114): <code>chunk_by_characters(file_path,relative_path,content,language) -&gt; Vec&lt;FileChunk&gt;</code> owns minified splitting. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:324)_
- `B005-F07-010`: — character algorithm (lines 115-130): iterate byte offset, cap provisional end at 2,000, scan backward to a safe delimiter when not at EOF, slice on a UTF-8 boundary, use <code>chunk_id(relative_path,offset)</code>, calculate start/end-line metadata from newline counts, and advance without overlap. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:325)_
- `B005-F07-011`: — cap behavior (lines 132-147): <code>apply_char_cap</code> mutates every oversized chunk by finding a safe boundary at 2,000 and truncating content there; it is the final operation on every strategy. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:326)_
- `B005-F07-012`: — dispatch order (lines 149-188): split lines/detect language; detect minified before AST; otherwise return capped single chunk for tiny files, capped AST regions when available, or capped line windows as final fallback; emit debug path and computed average on detection. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:327)_
- `B005-F07-013`: — detection event (lines 191-195): emit one <code>MinifiedFileChunked</code> per detected file with <code>{relative_path,char_count,chunk_count,avg_line_length}</code> and surface it under Indexing activity. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:328)_
- `B005-F07-014`: — provider defense/recovery evidence (lines 197-203): retain or add a provider token/character cap; if it fires after universal capping, log “chunk pretrunc fired — should not happen if MAX_CHUNK_CHARS configured correctly” so invariant regression is observable. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:329)_
- `B005-F07-015`: — produced/consumed symbols (lines 205-217): export constants, <code>is_minified</code>, <code>chunk_by_characters</code>, <code>apply_char_cap</code>, and <code>SsbActionType::MinifiedFileChunked</code>; audit <code>chunk_file_content</code>, <code>make_chunks_from_content</code>, and every other knowledge chunk producer for detect-first/cap-last behavior. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:330)_
- `B005-F07-016`: — reachability/stub bans (lines 218-228): execute in full indexing and watcher incremental updates; prohibit any chunk-return path after the cap; reference the max constant at both cap and provider boundary; B-31’s IndexingProgressPanel is the frontend pair. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:331)_
- `B005-F07-017`: — observable contract (lines 229-235): a 50K+ one-line fixture must emit <code>MinifiedFileChunked</code>, create at least twenty-five chunks, and persist no chunk over 2,000. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:332)_
- `B005-F07-018`: — deterministic retrieval checks (lines 237-270): unit tests cover detection/splitting/cap/UTF-8; the fixture creates at least twenty stored chunks; global max length is at most 2,000; search still finds minified substrings; at least one event exists per file; emoji input must not panic. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:333)_
- `B005-F07-019`: — acceptance invariants (lines 273-294): strict 500 threshold, delimiter scan, cap-last on all strategies, byte-offset IDs, UTF-8 safety, per-file event, regression fixtures, provider defense, unchanged-or-improved Phase-3K metrics, and zero non-test unwrap are required. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:334)_
- `B005-F07-020`: — unit test inventory (lines 295-312): named tests cover single-line detection, normal rejection, max size, safe delimiters, unique IDs, truncation, four-byte boundaries, SSB emission, dispatch selection, and cap coverage for giant AST regions. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:335)_
- `B005-F07-021`: — fixture inventory (lines 313-317): add 50K valid JS, 150K valid CSS, generated Go with long strings, and a 50K JS file containing a four-byte emoji every thousand characters. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:336)_
- `B005-F07-022`: — implementation footprint (lines 319-337): add chunking constants/detect/character/cap modules and fixtures; modify BM25 dispatch, knowledge exports, SSB action type, and B-31’s V2 IndexingProgressPanel with optional “Detected N minified files” text; create <code>B-32-decisions.md</code>. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:337)_
- `B005-F07-023`: — threshold/model rationale (lines 339-348): decision record must justify 500 as bundler-sensitive without catching legitimate long lines and verify 2,000 against 8,192-token nomic and 512-token Granite contexts, choosing the conservative smaller-model fit. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:338)_
- `B005-F07-024`: — truncation default (lines 349-351): default to truncating oversize AST/line chunks and discarding their suffix rather than split-and-retain; the latter needs a larger refactor. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:339)_
- `B005-F07-025`: — overlap default (lines 352-355): character chunks are non-overlapping by default because overlap is judged unhelpful for opaque minified content. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:340)_
- `B005-F07-026`: — skip flag default (lines 356-358): record a possible <code>ELAI_SKIP_MINIFIED=1</code>; default is off so vendored bundles remain searchable. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:341)_
- `B005-F07-027`: — side benefits (lines 360-371): bound provider cost/errors, keep vendored/generated code searchable, use an O(n) byte scan without parser allocation, and establish cap-last defense in depth. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:342)_
- `B005-F07-028`: — downstream (lines 373-379): B-31 shares the refactor, B-29 is independent, and B-35 reuses the chunker for artifacts. _(anchor: DEEP-B-005.discovery.md:343)_

- `SUMMARY/SUM-0254`: section=`B-32 - Adaptive/minified-file chunking - PLANNED` `chunk_by_characters` scans backward for newline, space, tab, semicolon, or comma; chunk ID is the byte offset, not a line number. _(anchor: 02-B-PLAN-SUMMARY.discovery.md:438)_

- `B35-007`: Manifest format: The source requires a choice between TOML knowledge.artifacts and project-root .elai_artifacts.json, recommends TOML, and later recommends JSON only as a SocratiCode-import fallback; no final choice is recorded (lines 87-98, 540-545). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:282)_

- `B35-009`: Example artifact classes: The canonical examples are database-schema, api-spec, ubiquitous-language, and k8s-manifests, with SQL/OpenAPI/domain/deployment descriptions that encode when agents should consult them (lines 99-120). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:284)_

- `B35-012`: Path security: Relative paths resolve against project_root and are rejected if canonical resolution escapes it, preventing arbitrary system-file reads (lines 130-132). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:287)_
- `B35-013`: Directory expansion: Directory artifacts recursively expand during indexing and obey the project’s existing .elai_ignore rules (lines 133-135). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:288)_

- `B35-016`: Index-state schema: ArtifactIndexState contains name, last_indexed_at, deterministic BTreeMap file_hashes, chunk_count, and ArtifactStatus (lines 156-162). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:291)_

- `B35-018`: Incremental index loop: index_artifact reads each expanded file, computes blake3, skips an unchanged hash, and rebuilds only changed files before persisting ArtifactIndexState (lines 171-192). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:293)_
- `B35-019`: Text chunking: Markdown, YAML, JSON, Terraform, and TOML use B-32 chunk_by_lines with CHUNK_SIZE = 50 plus apply_char_cap (lines 181-185). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:294)_
- `B35-020`: SQL chunking: SQL uses simple-regex boundaries at CREATE TABLE, CREATE VIEW, and CREATE INDEX rather than generic line windows (lines 182-184). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:295)_
- `B35-021`: Embedding document shape: Every chunk uses the existing embedding provider and a “context_artifact: {artifact_name}” prefix before content, then upserts into the project context index (lines 185-190). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:296)_
- `B35-022`: Context storage schema: context_chunks has id, artifact_name, relative_path, content, start_line, end_line, embedding, content_hash, and indexed_at; HNSW indexes embeddings and Tantivy indexes content (lines 193-200). _(anchor: DEEP-B-006.discovery.md:297)_

## System: E - Deep feature discovery sweep (UX/memory, orchestration, codegen, validation/RAG, inference, observability, vision/security/economics, CI/skills, planning/RL)

Family E is a 55-session post-B/C/D improvement sweep. Each E-N is a self-contained implementation prompt with a WIRING_CONTRACT, a relation label (DELTA / EXTENSION / REPLACEMENT), and a plan-recorded status. Deep discovery did not independently verify implementation against the codebase. Where the summary layer and an original plan disagree, original-source / newer-plan precedence sets the target state. Losing descriptions stay as Superseded bullets.

  - An AUDITOR override of REASONER stance emits sycophancy_pushback_detected and is acceptance-tested with a planted false claim. (`E-003/E003-E4-008`)

  - The suite anchors internal D-19..D-25 measures to contamination-resistant 2026 public benchmarks and makes harness-vs-model decomposition mandatory beside scores. (`E-003/E003-E9-001`)
  - Effort is three sessions; B-37 is required, B-23 optional, D-22 supplies calibration, D-19..D-25 are extended, and .elai_cc/benches/external plus paired-bootstrap gating are new. (`E-003/E003-E9-002`)
  - BenchmarkSuite exposes name, version, run(model,harness), and paired_bootstrap_significance(a,b); its registry holds eleven implementations. (`E-003/E003-E9-003`)
  - Core symbols are BenchmarkSuite, HarnessConfig, BenchmarkResult, paired_bootstrap_p(a,b,n_iter), and ds_cp_coverage(calib_set,shift_set,alpha). (`E-003/E003-E9-004`)
  - SWE-bench-Live pulls the latest 50 issues, uses a 24-hour HTTP cache, verifies content hash and temporal cutoff, and executes through the existing CLI run pipeline. (`E-003/E003-E9-005`)
  - SWE-bench-Live blocks promotion only when month-over-month loss exceeds two points and paired-bootstrap p<0.05, then emits SweBenchLiveRunCompleted. (`E-003/E003-E9-006`)
  - LiveCodeBench v6 uses a last-60-days slice, PerRoleRuntime, and code-generation, self-repair, and test-output-prediction subtasks. (`E-003/E003-E9-007`)
  - LiveCodeBench floors are 30% local and 45% cloud with per-language breakdown, emitting LiveCodeBenchRunCompleted. (`E-003/E003-E9-008`)
  - tau2-bench covers retail and telecom and grades policy adherence rather than successful outcome, so a policy-violating booking fails. (`E-003/E003-E9-009`)
  - tau2 floors are retail .70 cloud/.55 local and telecom .85 cloud/.55 local, separately reported with Tau2BenchRunCompleted. (`E-003/E003-E9-010`)
  - BFCL v3 uses a multi-turn, per-role function-calling slice, complements D-21, has a 70% floor, and emits BfclV3RunCompleted. (`E-003/E003-E9-011`)
  - GAIA L1/L2 uses the HAL framework and a contracts fixture; shipped promotion requires L1≥50% and L2≥30%, with GaiaRunCompleted. (`E-003/E003-E9-012`)
  - ClawsBench runs {model A,model B}×{harness X,harness Y} and decomposes two-way ANOVA variance into model, harness, and interaction effects. (`E-003/E003-E9-013`)
  - ClawsBench emits model_effect_pp/harness_effect_pp, accompanies every harness/scaffold diff, and forbids model attribution when model spread is under 10pp within a harness. (`E-003/E003-E9-014`)
  - PRMBench uses Deception Resistance and Circular Logic subsets, gates D-2 PPM at the published baseline, and emits PrmBenchRunCompleted. (`E-003/E003-E9-015`)
  - Sharma probes cover feedback flip, mimicry, answer flip, and false-claim agreement; flip rate under 15% gates auditor/planner persona changes and emits SycophancyProbeCompleted. (`E-003/E003-E9-016`)
  - Math floors use cleaned GSM8K-Platinum, never raw GSM8K, plus MATH-500; local floors are 90% and 50%, with MathFloorsCompleted. (`E-003/E003-E9-017`)

### E-12: Production Fullstack Codegen
- **Status**: planned (plan-recorded; not independently verified shipped)
- **Anchors**: DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L157, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L158, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L159, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L160, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L161, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L162, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L163, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L164, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L165, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L166, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L167, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L168, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L169, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L170
- **Composes with**: B-30, B-37, C-21, C-31, C-32, E-11, E-13, E-14, E-18
- **Behaviors**:
  - ProductionGrade codegen moves beyond compile/tests by adding framework conventions, RLS, secrets, OWASP, observability seeds, and consolidated deny-quality tooling. (`E-003/E003-E12-001`)
  - Effort is three sessions; B-30/B-37/C-21/C-31/C-32/E-11 are dependencies, E-13/E-14 are parallel, and FrameworkAdapter plus manifests are net-new extensions. (`E-003/E003-E12-002`)
  - Seven convention manifests are named: wasp, encore, redwoodsdk, t3, hono, fastapi, and nextjs-app-router. (`E-003/E003-E12-003`)
  - Each manifest is token-compact (<200 lines), plain text plus fenced YAML, and contains root config, route/auth/db/env conventions, scaffold command, linter/formatter/test defaults, dependency manifests, and banned patterns. (`E-003/E003-E12-004`)
  - Manifest bans include stale Tailwind-v3 classes in v4 projects, localStorage JWTs, production prisma/drizzle push, and hard-coded admin credentials. (`E-003/E003-E12-005`)
  - FrameworkProfile variants are Wasp, EncoreDev, RedwoodSdk, T3Stack, HonoEdge, FastApi, NextAppRouter, and Generic. (`E-003/E003-E12-006`)
  - FrameworkAdapter exposes scaffold(ProjectSpec)→FileSpec list, production_checklist(), and apply_lint_defaults(FilePlan). (`E-003/E003-E12-007`)
  - IdeaFramer ProjectClass deterministically selects a profile through PROJECT_CLASS_TO_FRAMEWORK/config. (`E-003/E003-E12-008`)
  - Defaults map SaaS→WaspOrEncore, ApiBackend→Hono, AiApp→HonoCloudflare, Marketplace→Encore, and ContentSite→Astro. (`E-003/E003-E12-009`)
  - secrets_scan runs gitleaks plus trufflehog with 30-second timeout. (`E-003/E003-E12-010`)
  - owasp_static runs semgrep p/owasp-top-ten with a 60-second timeout. (`E-003/E003-E12-011`)
  - rls_probe parses sqlite3/pg_dump output and flags CREATE TABLE without ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. (`E-003/E003-E12-012`)
  - auth_hardening checks HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite cookies, /auth rate limits, and absence of demo admin accounts. (`E-003/E003-E12-013`)
  - dep_audit runs npm audit, pip-audit, and cargo-audit with JSON output. (`E-003/E003-E12-014`)
  - otel_present requires Sentry.init and OTel resource attributes in the server entry. (`E-003/E003-E12-015`)
  - structured_logging performs grep plus fixture sanity validation of log format. (`E-003/E003-E12-016`)
  - axe_lighthouse uses lighthouse-ci, requires ≥95 on critical pages, and runs only when frontend_pair is non-null. (`E-003/E003-E12-017`)
  - tdd_fail_first inspects git history: a new test’s first commit is alone and the second adds implementation. (`E-003/E003-E12-018`)
  - integration_real_dep rejects integration tests that use an all-mock harness. (`E-003/E003-E12-019`)
  - migration_push_ban rejects production-path prisma db push and drizzle-kit push scripts. (`E-003/E003-E12-020`)
  - linter_clean runs Biome, Ruff, and Clippy with warnings denied. (`E-003/E003-E12-021`)
  - localstorage_jwt rejects token writes to browser localStorage. (`E-003/E003-E12-022`)
  - dockerfile_secrets rejects secret-bearing ENV and requires BuildKit secret mounts. (`E-003/E003-E12-023`)
  - iac_policy_as_code uses CrossGuard/Checkov and forbids global ingress, disabled PublicAccessBlock, and open S3 buckets. (`E-003/E003-E12-024`)
  - LevelAuditVerdict findings add fifteen categories: CSRF_MISSING, SECRET_LEAK, RLS_OFF, OWASP_TOP10, PACKAGE_HALLUCINATED, AUTH_WEAK, LINTER_DUPLICATE, LOCALSTORAGE_JWT, DEMO_CREDS, MIGRATION_PUSH, DOCKERFILE_ENV_SECRET, IAC_OPEN_INGRESS, AXE_FAIL, OTEL_MISSING, and INTEGRATION_ALL_MOCK. (`E-003/E003-E12-025`)
  - Scope planning must select a profile from config, read its complete manifest, produce a convention-respecting FilePlan, and convert banned patterns into first-occurrence INTERACTIVE MistakeBook blocks. (`E-003/E003-E12-026`)
  - Scaffold emits exactly one linter/formatter config per language and removes .eslintrc, .prettierrc, .flake8, setup.cfg flake8, and pyproject black/isort sections. (`E-003/E003-E12-027`)
  - Each legacy removal emits legacy_config_stripped and C-32 flush_to_disk performs one atomic write per file. (`E-003/E003-E12-028`)
  - SERVER_ENTRY_SEEDS is keyed by profile and adds 15-30 LOC of Sentry init, OTel attributes, and a structured logger only when dependency manifests permit the dependency. (`E-003/E003-E12-029`)

### E-18: Tool-Use Reliability
- **Status**: shipped (plan-recorded claim; deep pass did not independently verify)
- **Anchors**: DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L215, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L216, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L217, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L218, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L219, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L220, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L221, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L222, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L223, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L224, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L225, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L226, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L227, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L228
- **Composes with**: B-37, B-20, C-13, D-13, E-26, E-27, E-32, E-2, E-44
- **Behaviors**:
  - The tool path is hardened with XGrammar, a Hermes envelope, SEARCH/REPLACE fences, one-shot error-aware recovery, and ToolResult spill, addressing malformed JSON, escape bugs, retry loops, edit disorientation, package hallucination, and long responses. (`E-003/E003-E18-001`)
  - Effort is two-to-three sessions; B-7b and B-37 are shipped prerequisites, B-20 and C-13 are planned integration frames, and D-13 remains a later cross-family verifier. (`E-003/E003-E18-002`)
  - server.py replaces regex/in-house constraints with xgrammar.GrammarMatcher and a transformers LogitsProcessor. (`E-003/E003-E18-003`)
  - All fifteen IPC schemas plus tool schemas precompile at sidecar boot; any compile failure is a startup error, never a fallback. (`E-003/E003-E18-004`)
  - Grammar masking requires the Hermes <tool_call>...</tool_call> envelope and makes the known fenced-json fallback impossible at token selection. (`E-003/E003-E18-005`)
  - A Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-NF4 sidecar smoke fuzzes 100 tool prompts and requires 100% envelope presence. (`E-003/E003-E18-006`)
  - Edit tier one becomes SearchReplaceMatcher with exact fences <<< ELAI_SEARCH, === ELAI_REPLACE, and >>> ELAI_END. (`E-003/E003-E18-007`)
  - DelimiterCollisionGuard scans for the custom tokens and git conflict markers; any collision falls back to whole-file rewrite. (`E-003/E003-E18-008`)
  - Tier-2 validation failure or a SEARCH/REPLACE miss gets exactly one reprompt containing a structured <tool_error>; a second failure escalates to .claude/agents/fixer.md. (`E-003/E003-E18-009`)
  - A retry may never reuse the same prompt and can never loop beyond the single recovery attempt. (`E-003/E003-E18-010`)
  - Recovery emits tool_one_shot_recovered on success or tool_retry_exhausted after the capped attempt. (`E-003/E003-E18-011`)
  - ToolResult inline content is capped at 8K tokens; overflow writes .elai_cc/sessions/{id}/spill/{uuid}.txt and returns spill_ref. (`E-003/E003-E18-012`)
  - A spilled result emits tool_result_spilled. (`E-003/E003-E18-013`)
  - Before Edit/Bash touches Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml, or package.json, registry_check verifies package name and last-published age against crates.io/PyPI/npm. (`E-003/E003-E18-014`)

### E-26: Inference Engines 2026
- **Status**: shipped (plan-recorded claim; deep pass did not independently verify)
- **Anchors**: DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L263, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L264, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L265, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L266, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L267, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L268, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L269, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L270, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L271, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L272, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L273, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L274, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L275, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L276
- **Composes with**: B-37, E-2, E-27, E-32, E-54
- **Behaviors**:
  - E-26 feeds PS-4 routing economics through a SGLang throughput tier and Ollama demotion; the live $/verified-task leg remains blocked on J-28. (`E-003/E003-E26-001`)
  - The runtime policy is hybrid: SGLang for cloud planner/critic/structured JSON, custom Sidecar for research/DoLa/ETC/steering/TurboQuant, and Ollama deprecated but retained. (`E-003/E003-E26-002`)
  - B-37 is shipped prerequisite; S1-S4 are free-lane shippable, while S5 is gated on unresolved E-2 Part-3 plus RunPod. (`E-003/E003-E26-003`)
  - B-37’s eleven backends become twelve with Sglang; Vllm remains untouched and Sidecar’s processor chain remains canonical. (`E-003/E003-E26-004`)
  - Existing media-validator SglangConfig and new long-lived SglangRuntimeConfig are distinct lifecycle types and must not be collapsed. (`E-003/E003-E26-005`)
  - SglangBackend implements RuntimeAdapter over OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions and native /generate endpoints, with /v1/models health and SSE streaming. (`E-003/E003-E26-006`)
  - SglangRuntimeConfig contains base_url, optional api_key, request_timeout, and StructuredOutputBackend. (`E-003/E003-E26-007`)
  - StructuredOutputBackend variants are XGrammar, Outlines, and LMFE; response_format JSON schema and native regex are both supported. (`E-003/E003-E26-008`)
  - The adapter is HTTP-only and must not launch sgl-server; request-ID hashing uses blake3. (`E-003/E003-E26-009`)
  - Factory registration adds runtime/mod.rs module exposure, adapter enum/factory arms, resolve_backend("sglang"), and existing permission opt-in. (`E-003/E003-E26-010`)
  - With a healthy configured endpoint, planner, critic, prompt_engineer, and structured-JSON callers route to Sglang; research, executor, and memory_writer keep existing routes. (`E-003/E003-E26-011`)
  - If SGLang is unhealthy routing falls back to Sidecar; if ELAI_SGLANG_BASE_URL is unset behavior must exactly match B-37 defaults. (`E-003/E003-E26-012`)
  - RuntimeAdapter trait drift is handled by mirroring vllm; non-mechanical drift requires STOP/handoff rather than a stub. (`E-003/E003-E26-013`)
  - Ollama remains constructible and factory-resolvable but gains doc-hidden deprecation plus one construction warning citing the 19× throughput and 1.2GB RAM gap. (`E-003/E003-E26-014`)
  - rules/schema adds a dated WARN recommending Sidecar local or Sglang cloud; its tuple shape must follow neighboring schema rows. (`E-003/E003-E26-015`)

### E-27: Quantization 2026
- **Status**: planned (plan-recorded; not independently verified shipped)
- **Anchors**: DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L318, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L319, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L320, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L321, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L322, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L323, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L324, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L325, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L326, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L327, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L328, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L329, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L330, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L331
- **Composes with**: B-37, E-26, E-28, E-2
- **Behaviors**:
  - Serving evaluates AWQ+Marlin W4A16 and FP8 KV while preserving NF4 for QLoRA; migration order is FP8 KV, then AWQ, then a separate QLoRA checkpoint path. (`E-003/E003-E27-001`)
  - Effort is two sessions; B-37 is required, E-26 optional, and E-26/E-28/E-2 require coordinated server.py windows but are logically orthogonal. (`E-003/E003-E27-002`)
  - ELAI_QUANT_BACKEND is nf4|awq|fp16 and defaults to nf4 for backward compatibility; --quant-backend awq plumbs to it. (`E-003/E003-E27-003`)
  - AWQ loads through AwqConfig(version="marlin") on compute capability ≥8.0 and falls back to version="gemm" before Ampere. (`E-003/E003-E27-004`)
  - NF4 loading remains available and may not be deleted because it serves QLoRA fine-tuning. (`E-003/E003-E27-005`)
  - ELAI_KV_CACHE_DTYPE is fp16|fp8_e4m3|fp8_e5m2 and defaults to fp16. (`E-003/E003-E27-006`)
  - FP8 KV uses native hardware on Ada+ and a software-simulated path on Ampere. (`E-003/E003-E27-007`)
  - Ampere simulation emits kv_cache_dtype_software_sim and records the approximately 5% throughput cost. (`E-003/E003-E27-008`)
  - ModelCapabilityProfile gains quant_format and five VRAM-tier recommendations. (`E-003/E003-E27-009`)
  - The 8GB tier uses Qwen2.5-Coder-3B AWQ-Marlin with GGUF Q5_K_M fallback when AWQ is unavailable. (`E-003/E003-E27-010`)
  - The 12GB tier uses Qwen2.5-Coder-7B AWQ-Marlin plus FP8 KV. (`E-003/E003-E27-011`)
  - The 24GB tier targets Qwen2.5-Coder-14B AWQ-Marlin while EXL3 is deferred. (`E-003/E003-E27-012`)
  - The 48GB tier uses Qwen2.5-Coder-32B FP8 W8A8 on Ada+ or AWQ+FP8KV on Ampere. (`E-003/E003-E27-013`)
  - The 48GB+B200 tier reserves future NVFP4+QAD. (`E-003/E003-E27-014`)
  - ResearchTierConfig keeps NF4+FA2 only for QLoRA-eligible use and selects AWQ-Marlin+FA2+FP8KV for ≥12GB serving tiers. (`E-003/E003-E27-015`)
  - Five dated rules BLOCK AWQ without Marlin/Machete, sub-W4/W4A8 reasoning cliffs, and TurboQuant<4-bit KV; they WARN on NF4 beyond 40K and GGUF Q4_K_M for code. (`E-003/E003-E27-016`)
  - build_awq.py takes a checkpoint and default 256-line code calibration sample and creates a coexisting Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-AWQ checkpoint. (`E-003/E003-E27-017`)
  - autoawq must pass PyPI anti-slopsquatting verification before dependency addition. (`E-003/E003-E27-018`)
  - REMOTE-SIDECAR documents an alternate AWQ+fp8_e5m2 boot while retaining the NF4 boot as default. (`E-003/E003-E27-019`)
  - Five fixed prompt classes run at temperature zero under NF4 and AWQ; the gate requires HumanEval parity and token-cosine >.95 rather than byte equality. (`E-003/E003-E27-020`)
  - Long-context regression sweeps 8K/16K/25K, requires code-completion parity, and writes awq_vs_nf4_longctx.csv. (`E-003/E003-E27-021`)
  - Both features ship default-off for a telemetry week; 12GB+ defaults flip only in a later patch after tasks 8/9 pass three consecutive remote-3090 runs. (`E-003/E003-E27-022`)
  - E-27-decisions records W4A16, FP8-not-TurboQuant, Marlin-not-GPTQ-Marlin, NF4-QLoRA carve-out, and EXL3/NVFP4/MXFP4/TurboQuant non-goals. (`E-003/E003-E27-023`)
  - Produced identifiers are AwqMarlinLoader, Fp8KvCacheConfig, build script/tests, QuantBackendSelected, KvCacheDtypeSoftwareSim, AwqCheckpointBuilt, and five rule rows. (`E-003/E003-E27-024`)
  - Env boot selects weights/cache and emits SSB; build_awq creates the checkpoint through a separate user-invoked path. (`E-003/E003-E27-025`)
  - Stub bans forbid unimplemented Marlin, silent NF4 fallback, EXL3 imports, and TurboQuant<4-bit KV; no new frontend is required. (`E-003/E003-E27-026`)
  - The live artifact target is ≥3× NF4 tok/s, sustained 25K parity, and VRAM ≤2.0GB for 3B/≤4.5GB for 7B, with quant_backend_selected payload including backend, kv dtype, compute capability, and marlin flag. (`E-003/E003-E27-027`)
  - Deterministic checks verify env branches, build script, profiles, tier strings, rules, events, hardware tests, and decisions. (`E-003/E003-E27-028`)
  - Acceptance requires Marlin boot, native/sim FP8 evidence, five-prompt parity, 25K parity, held-out HumanEval non-regression, recorded tok/s on 3060/3090, preserved NF4, no deferred formats, event round-trip, and green hardware/workspace tests. (`E-003/E003-E27-029`)
  - Tests cover five-prompt parity, long-context sweep, native/sim cache behavior, event round-trip, and 12/24/48GB profile resolution. (`E-003/E003-E27-030`)
  - Four Python scripts/tests, two Rust contracts, and decisions are created; server, pyproject, profiles, tiers, rules, SSB, and remote boot docs are modified. (`E-003/E003-E27-031`)
  - Qwen-7B Marlin speed, long-context curve, and FP8 code impact are unmeasured; Ampere defaults FP8 off until parity evidence, and autoawq version must be reverified. (`E-003/E003-E27-032`)
  - EXL3, NVFP4/MXFP4, TurboQuant KV, and embedding-store TurboQuant are not adopted; future patches promote AWQ and add 14B/Blackwell lanes. (`E-003/E003-E27-033`)
  - Inferred: AWQ checkpoints can compose with future SGLang serving, but no SGLang model-loader changes are specified here. (`E-003/E003-E27-034`)
  - Ambiguity: The source says Ada+ uses native FP8 and Ampere simulation, but acceptance wording associates fp8_e5m2 with Ada+ without pinning which FP8 variant each architecture should prefer. (`E-003/E003-E27-035`)
  - Conflict: The orientation summary says “switch serving from NF4 to AWQ”; the original keeps nf4 as the default and AWQ default-off until a later three-run promotion. (`E-003/E003-E27-036`)
  - Conflict: 4.4× is cited from external 32B measurements and “identical HumanEval”; the implementation’s live target is ≥3× plus local parity, so 4.4× is not the immediate acceptance floor. (`E-003/E003-E27-037`)
  - Summary-delta: `ADDITION` (DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L604): Add all env/default/fallback semantics, five VRAM profiles, five policy rules, code-aware AWQ build, alternate boot, parity/long-context CSV tests, three-run telemetry rollout, exact events, hardware artifacts, and deferred formats. (`E-003/DELTA-E003-E27-01`)
  - Summary-delta: `CORRECTION` (DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L605): nf4/fp16 remain the default path initially; AWQ/FP8 are default-off and only a later patch promotes 12GB+ after three consecutive passes. (`E-003/DELTA-E003-E27-02`)
  - Summary-delta: `CORRECTION` (DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L606): The live acceptance target is ≥3× plus parity, not a guaranteed 4.4×; 4.4× is cited external evidence. (`E-003/DELTA-E003-E27-03`)
  - Summary-delta: `CORRECTION` (DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L607): awq_loaded, fp8_kv_active, and nf4_qlora_only are not source events; exact events are QuantBackendSelected, KvCacheDtypeSoftwareSim, and AwqCheckpointBuilt. (`E-003/DELTA-E003-E27-04`)

### E-32: Context Window Extension
- **Status**: planned (plan-recorded; not independently verified shipped)
- **Anchors**: DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L365, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L366, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L367, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L368, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L369, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L370, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L371, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L372, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L373, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L374, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L375, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L376, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L377, DEEP-E-003.discovery.md:L378
- **Composes with**: B-37, B-31, E-31, B-32, C-13
- **Behaviors**:
  - The plan combines a native 32K ceiling, training-free FITM calibration, an opt-in 64K DCA deep lane, and a loud rejection of YaRN on the default coder model. (`E-003/E003-E32-001`)
  - Effort is one-to-two sessions; B-37 and the knowledge engine exist, B-31 is parallel, E-31 supplies canonical VRAM gating, and no C/D plan overlaps FITM/context. (`E-003/E003-E32-002`)
  - Documentation currently presents 25K as hard ceiling and 20K production, while runtime_client’s code default is 131,072; E-32 changes docs/env guidance, not that code default. (`E-003/E003-E32-003`)
  - CLAUDE.md changes the documented hard ceiling to 32,000 and production guidance to 25,000-28,000 with grounded VRAM/model-card rationale. (`E-003/E003-E32-004`)
  - REMOTE-SIDECAR changes production/max guidance to 25K/32K and recomputes the 85% handoff point as 27,200 tokens. (`E-003/E003-E32-005`)
  - FoundInTheMiddleCalibrator runs only when prompt_len>8K and ELAI_FITM_ENABLED=1, using a second forward pass with a dummy replacement and subtracting positional prior. (`E-003/E003-E32-006`)
  - ELAI_FITM_DUMMY_TEXT defaults to a 50-token lorem block and no dummy may exceed 100 tokens. (`E-003/E003-E32-007`)
  - FITM inserts after existing DoLa/ETC/steering processors and is a no-op with no extra forward pass for prompts ≤8K. (`E-003/E003-E32-008`)
  - FITM defaults OFF and can become default-on only after an internal 20-50-trace RAG evaluation shows at least +5pp recall@3. (`E-003/E003-E32-009`)
  - Each applied calibration emits fitm_calibration_applied with prompt_len, dummy_len, and applied_ms. (`E-003/E003-E32-010`)
  - The sidecar Anthropic request gains a per-request fitm override, defaulting to environment configuration. (`E-003/E003-E32-011`)
  - ELAI_DEEP_MODE=1 on a box with at least 24GB loads Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M instead of the standard abliterated 7B. (`E-003/E003-E32-012`)
  - Deep mode enables DCA chunked prefill and hard-caps context at 64K. (`E-003/E003-E32-013`)
  - On less than 24GB deep mode is refused, falls back to standard mode, logs a warning, and must not crash. (`E-003/E003-E32-014`)
  - Successful deep-mode boot emits deep_mode_activated with model_id, ctx_cap, and vram_gb. (`E-003/E003-E32-015`)
  - At a SessionDag handoff, cross-file synthesis means more than three referenced files and no retrieval-localized answer; if a reachable 24GB box exists, local deep mode is preferred over cloud. (`E-003/E003-E32-016`)
  - The escalation emits deep_mode_escalation_chosen with reason and files_referenced. (`E-003/E003-E32-017`)
  - ELAI_USE_YARN=1 with Qwen2.5-Coder raises a cited SidecarBootError and instructs use of DCA deep mode instead. (`E-003/E003-E32-018`)
  - The YaRN refusal path emits YarnRefused/yarn_refused; loud refusal with no silent fallback is acceptance-required. (`E-003/E003-E32-019`)
  - run_fitm_eval.py reads 20-50 workflow/session retrieval traces, compares FITM on/off recall@3 and recall@5 locally, and writes dated JSON results. (`E-003/E003-E32-020`)
  - Handoff threshold is 85% of sidecar-reported effective_max_context and may not hard-code 20K, 25K, or 32K. (`E-003/E003-E32-021`)
  - A-MEM Zettelkasten memory is deferred because it overlaps B-31/B-32 knowledge and symbol graphs. (`E-003/E003-E32-022`)
  - E-32-decisions records 32K-vs-YaRN, the +5pp FITM gate, 24GB cross-file deep-mode gating, and explicit non-goals YaRN, StreamingLLM, Ring Attention, Infini-attention, and 1M serving. (`E-003/E003-E32-023`)
  - Produced identifiers are FoundInTheMiddleCalibrator, activate_deep_mode, refuse_yarn_at_boot, deep_mode_escalation_hook, four SSB variants, and the FITM evaluation scaffold. (`E-003/E003-E32-024`)
  - The sidecar processor chain, Sidecar request passthrough, grounding-client threshold, boot checks, long-request calibration, and handoff escalation form the reachability paths. (`E-003/E003-E32-025`)
  - Stub bans prohibit reachable YaRN, hard-coded context thresholds, oversized dummy text, deep boot below 24GB, untyped boundary errors, and non-blake3 cache hashing. (`E-003/E003-E32-026`)
  - RuntimePanel shows effective_max_context and deep-mode status. (`E-003/E003-E32-027`)
  - A 27,200-token four-file smoke with FITM and a 24GB remote expects calibration, escalation, activation, 32K telemetry, and an AuditTimeline handoff event. (`E-003/E003-E32-028`)
  - Deterministic checks validate docs, calibrator, deep activation, YaRN refusal, four event arms, eval scaffold, dynamic threshold, and an end-to-end FITM SSB row. (`E-003/E003-E32-029`)
  - Acceptance requires docs, processor order, per-long-request evidence, 24GB DCA boot/refusal, escalation and refusal evidence, dynamic threshold, decisions, short-request no-op, no unwrap, and blake3. (`E-003/E003-E32-030`)
  - Tests cover ≤8K no-op/>8K extra pass/bounded delta, YaRN typed failure, 24GB activation/12GB fallback, FITM/deep SSB schema, and dynamic handoff. (`E-003/E003-E32-031`)
  - CLAUDE/remote docs, server, escalation policy, Sidecar, grounding client, SSB, and RuntimePanel are modified; FITM eval and decisions are created. (`E-003/E003-E32-032`)
  - Risks are unmeasured 12GB 32K VRAM, workload-specific FITM lift, slow deep boot, mock-sidecar compatibility, a hard YaRN break, A-MEM overlap, and local-deep-vs-cloud policy. (`E-003/E003-E32-033`)
  - If sidecar effective_max_context is unavailable, threshold logic may use a sane 25K compatibility fallback. (`E-003/E003-E32-034`)
  - A-MEM and PINE are deferred; B-31 must avoid double FITM, C-13 consumes events, and E-31 must receive the 24GB deep-mode row. (`E-003/E003-E32-035`)
  - Inferred: FITM and deep-mode escalation can occur in one long request sequence, but state transfer between the standard and deep sidecars is not specified. (`E-003/E003-E32-036`)
  - Ambiguity: “Refuse to boot deep mode” and “fall back to standard mode” coexist; the operative acceptance behavior is non-crashing fallback, but whether the process reports boot success or a typed recoverable error is unspecified. (`E-003/E003-E32-037`)
  - Conflict: The title/objective says lift 25K→32K, while the current documented production setting is 20K and runtime code defaults to 131,072; this is a documentation/effective-policy lift, not a single code constant change. (`E-003/E003-E32-038`)
  - Conflict: The orientation summary omits the 64K Qwen-1M DCA deep-mode lane and handoff escalation, both major original features. (`E-003/E003-E32-039`)
  - Conflict: The orientation summary invents context_lifted_32k and fitm_recall_lift_measured events and a 15pp target; the original events are FitmCalibrationApplied/DeepModeActivated/DeepModeEscalationChosen/YarnRefused and its deployment gate is measured +5pp on ELAI data. ### E-36: Document Vision RAG
- **Status**: planned
- **Anchors**: DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L235, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L236, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L237, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L238, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L239, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L240, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L241, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L242, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L243, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L244, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L245, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L246, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L247, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L248
- **Composes with**: B-42, B-35, B-37, E-17, C-7, E-39, E-0
- **Behaviors**:
  - **PLANNED, 3 sessions/10-14h.** Adds an opt-in vision side to B-42 Cosmos/B-35 ArtifactCheck/B-37 runtimes and requires E-17 RRF; C-7 SSB substrate must land first. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-001`)
  - Text RAG remains primary for grep-able content. Vision retrieval is additive only for diagrams/scans/screens/slides; VLM captions are retrieval evidence, never authoritative grounding. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-002`)
  - Extends - not replaces - Cosmos. Adds `doc_parser` backends and `vision_verifier`; expands E-17 fusion from three to four lists; adds five vision SSB types; schema pin is deliberately TBD at execution. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-003`)
  - `elai doctor knowledge-models --vision` probes presence, tokenizer hash and size. Default `[knowledge.vision_retriever] model="colmodernvbert"`; alternate ColQwen2.5-v0.2; models live under `models_dir_path()`. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-004`)
  - `VisionChunk={source_blake3,page_idx,multi_vec:Vec<[f16;128]>,pooled,vlm_caption,parser_confidence}`; pool ~1,030 vectors to ~100 (≤128 contract), store in project SQLite `vision_chunks` keyed by source blake3. The cited pooling algorithm must be verified first. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-005`)
  - `PdfStructuredChunker` uses PaddleOCR-VL via `doc_parser` and returns markdown, HTML tables, figure crops, page confidences and `fallback_recommended`. Markdown goes to text chunking, figures to image chunking; any page confidence <0.85 forces image indexing. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-006`)
  - Cosmos gains `Diagram`, `ArchImage`, `Screenshot`, `ScannedDoc` schemas. Diagram stale-checks source **or** render; the other three stale-check source-file blake3. `ParserBackend` includes Paddle/MinerU/Dolphin plus three cloud parsers. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-007`)
  - Visual-spatial claims dispatch to `GroundingMethod::VisualArtifactCheck`: top-k image retrieval then Qwen2.5-VL structured `{verdict:Confirm | Refute | Indeterminate,evidence_pages,reliability:VlmCaption | OcrParse | DiagramSource}`. Consumers must downweight VLM-caption reliability. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-008`)
  - `RrfFusion4` uses default weights `{bm25:1.0,code_vec:1.0,text_vec:0.8,vision_vec:0.6}`, emits `rrf_vision_component_weight`, and omits the vision list when disabled. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-009`)
  - `[knowledge.vision_rag] enabled=false` is a hard shipping default. Disabled ingest stores caption+hash for visually rich inputs but skips multi-vectors; enabled stores the index. `VisionRagPolicyDecision` records enabled/budget/actual storage. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-010`)
  - Cloud parser fallback threshold defaults .7 and is eligible only outside `--mode local`; local refuses and logs `DocParserCloudFallbackBlockedByMode`; cloud cost consumes task spend ceiling. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-011`)
  - Separate 50-query gold set evaluates ColModernVBERT vs ColQwen at nDCG@5/Recall@5/MRR. At least one backend must reach nDCG@5≥.50 before any policy default-enables vision. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-012`)
  - CosmosDrawer extension or `VisionRAGDrawer` shows index state, storage, parse confidence and latest verdict/reliability; Tauri exposes `get_vision_artifact_status` and `get_vision_artifact_check_recent`. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-013`)
  - Wiring exports chunkers/schemas/artifact types/parser enum/verdict/reliability/RRF4, doctor probe and five events: `VisionChunkEmitted`, `VisionFallbackTriggered`, `VisualArtifactCheckVerdict`, `VisionRagPolicyDecision`, `DocParserCloudFallbackBlockedByMode`. Entry points are CLI, query pipeline, Tauri and verification dispatch. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-014`)
  - Negative contract: no unwrap, non-blake3 file hash, caption-only authority, full 1,030-vector storage, auto-enable, MarkItDown for image PDFs, Nougat, or local-mode cloud fallback. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-015`)
  - Smoke verifies an auth-diagram redirect claim and requires chunk/check/RRF rows, blake3-keyed database row, nonempty pages on determinate verdicts and a four-stage query trace. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-016`)
  - Deterministic checks cover hashes, enum+dispatch, four artifact types, parser registration, pooling cap, default-off config, five SSB variants, RRF4, two eval files and staged-model doctor output. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-017`)
  - Done gates require staged hash/size, working Paddle confidence, ≤25KB/page pooled storage, correct stale policy, routed reliability-aware verdict, opt-in RRF participation, mode/threshold fallback, .50 corpus nDCG and blake3-only code. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-018`)
  - Tests cover visual-vs-file dispatch, pooling recall within ±2 points, low/high parser confidence, LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH reliability mapping, three-run stable four-list ordering, diagram-render staleness and corpus nDCG gate. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-019`)
  - File lifecycle creates two chunkers, verifier, optional/new drawer, eval corpus/driver, five contracts and decision doc; modifies Cosmos, pipeline, verification, runtime, SSB, doctor, Tauri and config docs. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-020`)
  - Pooling citation is unverified; if absent, use measured max/mean pooling. Target budget is 25KB/page and suggested project default 500MB; emit over-budget evidence. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-021`)
  - Local VRAM cannot hold coder+VLM concurrently; captioning is ingest-time batch or remote billable sidecar that must be stopped after use. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-022`)
  - Do not default-enable without local-corpus .50 nDCG; all downstream gates must inspect reliability; cloud multimodal reranking is deferred; C-7 blocks entry if not shipped. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-023`)
  - Next: compose B-35+E-17 for text/vision retrieval; defer cloud reranking, reasoning-tier ColBERT and vision-chunk PageRank; coordinate cloud parse spend with E-39. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E36-024`)
  - Interaction: E-36 consumes C-7 Cosmos events, B-35 ArtifactCheck registry, B-37 roles and E-17 RRF; C-7 can block entry, and E-39 must govern cloud parse spend. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-INT-008`)
  - Interaction: Visual grounding combines image retrieval with a runtime VLM, but reliability tier controls downstream auditor/scope-planner weight and local mode can forbid cloud parsing. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-INT-009`)
  - Inferred: Mixed PDF ingest likely parses text/tables, crops figures, conditionally indexes image multi-vectors, then fuses four retrieval lists and verifies visual claims; atomic steps are explicit but transaction/partial-failure recovery is absent. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-INF-005`)
  - Ambiguity: “8th GroundingMethod” counting is unstable: FILE/SOURCE/TEST/WEB/API/API_REGISTRY + ArtifactCheck + CosmosCheck already names eight before VisualArtifactCheck; `VerificationMethod` versus `GroundingMethod` naming also shifts. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-AMB-010`)
  - Ambiguity: Pool-to-~100 algorithm is contingent on verifying a cited paper; fallback max/mean method and recall selection rule are not chosen. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-AMB-011`)
  - Ambiguity: Storage budget records a 500MB suggested default, but task schema names only budget/actual and does not specify eviction/rejection when exceeded. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-AMB-012`)
  - Conflict: E-36:47 vs E-36:57 | Page confidence <.85 forces image indexing; cloud fallback threshold defaults .7. Pages in [.7,.85) get vision indexing without cloud parse, which may be intentional but the two “fallback” labels can be mistaken as one rule. Preserve as two distinct gates.   - MoE is treated as the frontier trend; dense Qwen remains valid at 7-12GB but no adapter may encode dense-only assumptions. Future MoE-on-Ampere expert offload is documented, not implemented. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E38-002`)

### E-42: Tree-Sitter Grammars 2026
- **Status**: planned
- **Anchors**: DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L294, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L295, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L296, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L297, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L298, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L299, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L300, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L301, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L302, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L303, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L304, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L305, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L306, DEEP-E-001.discovery.md:L307
- **Composes with**: B-30, B-29, B-26
- **Behaviors**:
  - **PLANNED, 3 sessions/10-12h.** Refines planned B-30 and stabilizes the grammar substrate beneath in-flight B-29; changes `crates/knowledge/src/dkg/`, not chunk-level logic. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-001`)
  - Core target is 0.26.x/ABI 15. Grammars are maturity-tiered; composite parsing is one-level outer+injected reparse; Svelte 5 support is explicitly best-effort; Python `tree-sitter-language-pack` is forbidden in Rust. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-002`)
  - Cargo exact-pin instruction is `tree-sitter="=0.26"` in every importing crate, documented in `grammars.md`, with `cargo tree` verification against transitive bumps. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-003`)
  - `assert_abi_compatibility` calls the 0.26 language-version API for every loaded grammar, accepts versions **14 or 15**, fails fast with actionable error otherwise, and emits per-grammar `GrammarAbiProbeResult`. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-004`)
  - TIER-A registration claims “canonical 15” but enumerates rust, python, typescript, tsx, javascript, go, java, c, c-sharp, ruby, php, bash, html, css, json, yaml, toml, markdown; individual canonical crates are verified before addition; Markdown is CommonMark+GFM, never MDX. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-005`)
  - `experimental_grammars` gates kotlin, scala, swift, svelte, vue and optional C++; each load emits `GrammarTierBLoaded` with “may emit ERROR nodes.” Kotlin must be the `fwcd/tree-sitter-kotlin` grammar, not bindings. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-006`)
  - Svelte precheck detects `$state/$derived/$effect/$props`; tree walk counts ERROR+MISSING. With runes and ERROR rate >5%, downgrade that file to raw-text chunks and warn; emit `SvelteRunesParseHealth {file,error_node_count,missing_node_count,runes_detected}`. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-007`)
  - HTML/Svelte/Vue `injections.scm` maps script body→TypeScript and style→CSS and explicitly stops at one injection level. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-008`)
  - Experimental Astro split parses `---` frontmatter as TS and body as HTML/JS injections; RSC directives are ordinary TS syntax and have a TIER-A clean-parse regression test. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-009`)
  - Existing minified guard is average line length >500; add hard >2MB raw-text fallback and `TreeSitterSkippedLargeFile`; no parser rows for such input. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-010`)
  - Webview/WASM grammar path is guarded as unsupported because only Wasmtime is fully supported; predicted 1.5-2× slowdown is acceptable offline, not real-time; attempted load emits `tree_sitter_wasm_unsupported`. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-011`)
  - Regenerate `elai.map` with SCIP indices; previously supported languages must retain row count within ±5% and no SCIP_DEF/SCIP_REF regression. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-012`)
  - Wiring exports ABI types/functions, TIER-A/B registration and Svelte health plus four declared SSB enum variants. `DkgEngine::build_graph` is entry; CLI indexing flows through it. Smoke covers rs/py/ts/runes-Svelte/>2MB JSON and writes grammar-version audit. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-013`)
  - Dependency matrix names 17 TIER-A crates (TS crate also supplies TSX) and five TIER-B crates; mapper is a post-change consumer. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-014`)
  - Negative contract forbids language-pack, wrong core range, unwrap around ABI, ungated TIER-B, claims of full Svelte 5 support and MDX advertising. GrammarHealthPanel is optional/B-26-gated. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-015`)
  - Deterministic checks require exact pin, ABI definition+call, registration functions/cfg, no meta-dep/MDX, four SSB types, fwcd pin and a one-row-per-grammar audit artifact. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-016`)
  - Done gates require builds with/without feature, all ABI 14/15 rows, >5% raw fallback, >2MB skip, comprehensive `grammars.md`, mapper ±5%, no meta-dep/unwrap and an audit table with name/crate/version/ABI/tier/fork URL. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-017`)
  - Tests cover valid/invalid ABI, four runes/no false-positive, >5% fallback, 3MB skip, HTML injection, MDX non-crash without support, tier counts and kotlin fork pin. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-018`)
  - File lifecycle creates ABI/Svelte modules, `grammars.md`, shared injection query, audit and decision docs; modifies DKG, Cargo and SSB; dashboard panel remains optional. (`E-001/DEEP-E001-E42-019`)
